title: Yesterday
vocabFocus: Past basics: fui, hice, comí, vi, tuve
practiceFocus: Tell the story of what you did yesterday

points.title: Memorise the words, not the tense
points.rule: Ayer puts the story in the past. No still goes before the verb. Learn each past word next to the chunk you already say: fui with voy, hice with hago, comí with como, tuve with tengo, and estuve with estoy. Trabajé and cené are the one regular pattern worth copying: an -ar “I” form ends in -é. Fue means it was, next to es.

examples.english: I did. I ate. I saw. I had.
I did not go home early.

examples.spanish: Fue un día largo. Estuve en casa.
examples.english: It was a long day. I was at home.

grammar.notYet: The preterite chart, the imperfect, and every other past form.

phrases.english: I did not go home early.

phrases.spanish: Por la noche cené con amigos.
phrases.english: At night I had dinner with friends.

phrases.note: The past of es for a finished day.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Por la mañana fui al trabajo. Tuve muchas reuniones.
lines.english: In the morning I went to work. I had many meetings.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Hice ejercicio y después comí en casa.
lines.english: I worked out and then I ate at home.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.spanish: Por la noche vi una película. Fue muy buena.
lines.english: At night I watched a film. It was very good.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Qué bien. Yo estuve cansado. Fue un día largo.
lines.english: Nice. I was tired. It was a long day.

practice.title: Yesterday in three parts
practice.instruction: Tell morning, afternoon, and night. Use fui, hice, comí, vi, or tuve at least once each if you can.
tips: Learn these past words as chunks next to voy, hago, como, and tengo.
Keep the story moving. Do not recite a tense chart.
